content: Compass Community Services is a non-profit organization based in San Francisco, California, dedicated to providing a comprehensive range of support services to homeless and extremely low-income families. Through its four programs—Clara House, Compass Family Center, Connecting Point, and Tenderloin Childcare Center—Compass Community Services assists over 3,000 clients annually. The organization, originally known as Travelers Aid San Francisco, was established in 1914 to support newcomers to the city, particularly young women and girls drawn by the Panama-Pacific International Exposition in 1915. Over the years, Compass has served diverse populations, including stranded travelers, refugees, and homeless families, all of whom share a common need for assistance in navigating the challenges of an often inhospitable urban environment. In 1976, recognizing the growing demand for respite childcare among families utilizing its services, Compass opened the Tenderloin Childcare Center (TLC). Homeless children face developmental delays at four times the rate of other children, with nearly 50% experiencing emotional issues such as anxiety and depression. In 2002, TLC moved into its own building, enabling the center to enroll 72 children and, for the first time, offer infant care. TLC’s expertise in addressing the needs of this population allows for prompt identification and intervention when developmental or emotional issues arise in its students. In response to the escalating crisis of family homelessness, Compass launched the Compass Family Center (CFC) in 1990, an emergency shelter program providing short-term housing, counseling, referrals, and assistance in securing permanent housing. By 1995, the program expanded to include aftercare services, pre-employment support, and psychotherapy. In 2006, CFC received a three-year grant from the SF First Five Commission to implement the Positive Parenthood Project, which offers parent-child services aimed at improving developmental outcomes for children aged 0-5. In 2007, CFC, in partnership with Catholic Charities CYO, was awarded a contract to provide housing subsidies to families who are homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness. This initiative adheres to the housing first principle, prioritizing rapid rehousing or housing retention to prevent families from entering the cycle of homelessness. The program, known as SF HOME, also provides intensive services to help families increase their income through employment and training. In 1995, Compass Community Services established Clara House, a long-term supportive housing program. Families in this program are given the opportunity to live in a stable, service-enriched environment for up to two years while preparing to transition to permanent housing. Initially, the program faced challenges due to Proposition 187, which barred undocumented individuals from accessing publicly funded employment services—a key component of Clara House. Ultimately, the program decided to remove legal immigration status as a requirement for admission, ensuring inclusivity for all families in need. At the request of and with funding from the San Francisco Human Services Agency, Compass launched Connecting Point (CP) in 1995. This program serves as the central intake and assessment center for any family in San Francisco seeking access to the city’s shelter system. In 2007, CP partnered with the Eviction Defense Collaborative to provide rental assistance, enabling families to maintain housing and avoid homelessness.
